name: Confirm Placement Details
description: Agree tasks, dates, and hours with the studio; confirm your technical mentor and repo access.
flavor: Clear specs prevent scope creep.

name: Complete Dev Onboarding
description: Set up IDE, clone repos, configure build pipeline, and review coding standards.
flavor: Environment ready. Code awaits.

name: Implement a Gameplay Feature
description: Write clean, tested code for a mechanic, system, or tool. Follow the studio's patterns.
flavor: Code that compiles is just the start.

name: Log Dev Hours & Reflection
description: Record hours and reflect on technical challenges, debugging, and architecture decisions.
flavor: Commit messages tell the real story.

name: Technical Reflection
description: Write a reflection on your implementation: performance, maintainability, and lessons learned.
flavor: Reflection turns bugs into wisdom.

name: Feature Shipped
description: Your code is in a playable build. Document the feature and its player-facing impact.
flavor: Shipped code is the only code that matters.

name: Measure Technical Impact
description: Explain how your code improved performance, stability, or developer velocity.
flavor: Metrics validate engineering.

name: Book Studio Tech Visit
description: Arrange a visit to a studio's engineering team. Confirm date, NDA, and tech stack overview.
flavor: See how pros architect game systems.

name: Attend Code Review / Tech Talk
description: Sit in on a code review, architecture discussion, or engine deep-dive.
flavor: Watch how seniors think in code.

name: Find Game Jam Dev Role
description: Join a game jam or student project as a programmer. Confirm tech stack and team needs.
flavor: Game jams are dev bootcamps.

name: Program for a Game Jam
description: Implement core systems, gameplay code, or tools for a 48-hour game jam project.
flavor: Constraints breed elegant solutions.

name: Game Jam Code Review
description: Collect feedback from teammates on your code quality, architecture, and collaboration.
flavor: Jam code reviews are brutally honest.

name: Understand the Technical Brief
description: Clarify the brief: target platform, performance budget, engine version, and deliverables.
flavor: A brief understood prevents rewrites.

name: Deliver Technical Implementation
description: Build the requested system, tool, or feature. Profile, optimise, and iterate on feedback.
flavor: Working code > perfect architecture.

name: Document Technical Learnings
description: Write a post-mortem: what worked, performance results, and what you'd refactor.
flavor: Every brief teaches a new constraint.

name: Partner Technical Requirements
description: Agree on technical deliverables with an industry partner: API, tool, or engine feature.
flavor: Partners want solutions that integrate cleanly.

name: Complete Partner Technical Task
description: Deliver a robust, documented implementation for the industry partner.
flavor: Professional code review sharpens your craft.

name: Showcase Partner Implementation
description: Present your partner work with context: requirements, architecture, testing, and results.
flavor: Show the engineering, not just the feature.

name: Partner Code Adopted
description: Your implementation was merged, shipped, or influenced the partner's technical direction.
flavor: Merged PRs beat hypotheticals every time.

name: Agree Dates & Schedule
description: Confirm the schedule and hours in writing. Must fit college hours (8:30am–5:30pm, max 8hr day).
flavor: Verbal agreements evaporate. Written ones stick.

name: Agree Your Dev Role
description: Clarify responsibilities: gameplay, engine, tools, AI, graphics, or full-stack.
flavor: Undefined dev work is technical debt waiting to happen.

name: Dev Mentor Contact
description: Get a named technical mentor and a way to reach them — email, Slack, or GitHub.
flavor: A senior dev's time is the best resource you'll have.

name: Find a Studio
description: Identify a studio whose tech stack and game genre match your interests.
flavor: Build for games you'd want to play.

name: Complete Programming Assignment
description: Finish a course assignment demonstrating programming skills relevant to your target role.
flavor: Grades open doors. Engineering skills keep them open.

name: Refactor After Feedback
description: Improve code using specific review feedback. Shows growth mindset and craftsmanship.
flavor: First pass works. Second pass lasts.

name: Ask for a Dev Reference
description: Request written feedback from a lead programmer or technical mentor.
flavor: A reference is a vote of confidence in writing.

name: Write a Dev CV Bullet
description: Describe your technical contribution, the problem solved, and measurable impact.
flavor: Don't list features. List technical outcomes.

name: Daily Dev Log
description: Record what you built, what you debugged, and what you learned each day.
flavor: Code unrecorded is knowledge lost.

name: Technical Distinction Earned
description: Bonus evidence: your code was recognised for excellence or innovation.
flavor: Excellence isn't accidental. It's engineered.

name: Save Code Portfolio Piece
description: Keep a finished system, tool, or GitHub repo and explain your role and architecture.
flavor: Your GitHub is your proof. Make it readable.

name: Travel & Studio Access Plan
description: Check location, travel, hardware needs, VPN access, and any studio requirements.
flavor: The best plan fails if you can't clone the repo.

name: Wild Card: Senior Dev Mentor
description: A senior developer guides your approach. Use in place of any Setup, Action, or Proof card for a Live Project Brief.
flavor: The best engineers had mentors first.

name: Wild Card: Careers Team
description: Careers team connects you with a programming placement. Use in place of any Setup, Action, or Proof card for a Block Placement.
flavor: They know which studios hire junior devs.

name: Wild Card: Code Review
description: A thorough code review strengthens your evidence. Use in place of a Proof card for a Block Placement.
flavor: Fresh eyes catch what you missed.

name: Wild Card: Extended Sprint
description: Extra time to polish your implementation. Use in place of an Action card for a Live Project Brief.
flavor: Great code needs iteration time.

name: Wild Card: Tutor Code Review
description: A quick code check-in with your tutor. Use in place of a Setup card for Volunteering.
flavor: Sometimes the right question prevents a bug.
